column1: # Playlist parse cases (B430): the ONE table the iOS importer (PlaylistImport) and the
# bridge's future indexer (backlog B431) must both pass. The iOS copy is canonical; when the
# bridge gains its copy, keep the two byte-identical and change both in one Mirror-PR pair.
# Scope: decoding, line splitting, the skipped lines and the path rule. NOT the library lookup:
# "resolved" means the path rule places the entry inside the share; whether a row exists there,
# and case or Unicode folding against stored paths, happen after this and are not tested here.
# Not covered on purpose (docs/PlaylistFileImportStudy.md section 8, PR 4 trimmed): absolute
# paths, drive letters, UNC paths and URLs. Their handling is not settled, so nothing pins it.
# Columns are tab-separated: case, playlist, input, resolved, unresolved.
#   playlist    the playlist file's own path, relative to the share root (no leading "/").
#   resolved    the entries the path rule places, in file order, as paths relative to the
#               share root, separated by "|". Duplicates are kept. Empty: none.
#   unresolved  the entry lines the path rule cannot place inside the share, in file order,
#               separated by "|", each trimmed and with "\" folded to "/". Empty: none.
# Every column but case is escaped: \n LF, \r CR, \t TAB, \\ a backslash, \xNN the byte NN
# (two hex digits). Any other byte stands for itself; a literal "|" in a path is \x7C.
# Decode input to bytes and feed them to the parser. Decode the other columns to bytes and
# compare them with the UTF-8 bytes of the parser's output: byte-for-byte, so an NFC and an
# NFD spelling of one name are different paths.
#   - A UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) at the start is dropped as bytes, before any decoding. Encoding
#     is then decided for the whole file: UTF-8 if every byte is valid UTF-8, else Windows-1252
#     if no byte is one it leaves undefined (81, 8D, 8F, 90, 9D), else ISO-8859-1, which maps
#     each byte to the code point of its value and cannot fail (B437): ASCII lines always
#     survive, and a name in another code page stays mojibake.
#   - Lines end at LF, CRLF or CR. Each line is trimmed of whitespace at both ends.
#     (The app's splitter also ends a line at U+0085 and U+2028, so in a file decoded as
#     ISO-8859-1 the byte 85 ends a line too; no row pins either.)
#   - A blank line, or a line whose first non-blank character is "#", is not an entry.
#   - "\" is folded to "/". A path is relative to the playlist's folder. "." segments are
#     dropped, ".." pops a segment, and a ".." with nothing left to pop puts the entry outside
#     the share (unresolved), even if later segments come back down. Empty segments collapse.
#   - Bytes are kept: no Unicode normalization and no case folding.
